about: Saudi-based buy now pay later fintech allowing consumers to split purchases into instalments at online and in-store merchants across Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Kuwait, alongside shopping and card products. Earns merchant fees and consumer fees, with millions of users and thousands of partner retailers. Headquartered in Riyadh; founded 2020. Backed by investors such as Sanabil, Checkout.com and Shorooq; became a unicorn after a 2023 debt financing. Well-known consumer brand in the Gulf and an active regional sports and event sponsor.

Global mobility and delivery platform operating Uber ride-hailing, Uber Eats food and grocery delivery, Uber Freight and autonomous vehicle partnerships. Earns commissions from drivers, couriers and merchants plus advertising and subscriptions (Uber One), serving well over 150 million monthly users in more than 70 countries. Headquartered in San Francisco, California; founded 2009. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (UBER) with revenue around 40 to 50 billion dollars. Household consumer brand worldwide and a sports sponsor in football and other leagues.

wiki.title: Uber
wiki.text: Uber Technologies, Inc. is an American multinational transportation company that provides ride-hailing services, courier services, food delivery, and freight transport. It is headquartered in San Francisco, California, and operates in approximately 70 countries and 15,000 cities worldwide. It is the largest ridesharing company worldwide with over 202 million monthly active users and 10 million active drivers and couriers. It coordinates an average of 42 million trips and delivery orders per day, and has coordinated 72 billion trips and delivery orders since its inception in 2010. In the fourth quarter of 2025, the company had a take rate of 2

about: Social media platform formerly known as Twitter, for short posts, news, video and live conversations, now with Grok AI and X Premium subscriptions, and part of Elon Musk's xAI group after a 2025 merger. Earns from advertising and subscriptions with several hundred million monthly users. Operating base listed in San Francisco, with Bastrop, Texas shown in the input. Acquired by Elon Musk for 44 billion dollars in 2022 and delisted; private. Global mass-market brand, though advertisers have been cautious since the takeover.

wiki.title: X (social network)
wiki.text: X, formerly known as Twitter, is an American microblogging and social networking service, headquartered in Bastrop, Texas, and owned by X Corp., a subsidiary of SpaceXSI, a subsidiary of the technology company SpaceX. It is one of the world's largest social media platforms and one of the most-visited websites. Users can share short text messages, images, and videos in short posts and like other users' content. The platform also includes direct messaging, video and audio calling, bookmarks, lists, communities, Grok chatbot integration, job search, and a social audio feature. Users can vote on context added by approved users using the Community

wiki.title: X
wiki.what: Twenty-fourth letter of the Latin alphabet
wiki.text: X is the twenty-fourth letter of the Latin alphabet, used in the modern English alphabet, the alphabets of other western European languages and others worldwide. Its name in English is ex, plural exes.

about: Saudi-Emirati e-commerce platform launched in 2017 by Mohamed Alabbar, backed by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, offering electronics, fashion, groceries and home goods through the noon app and noon Minutes, plus Namshi fashion and noon Food. Operates in the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Egypt, with tens of millions of customers. Headquarters listed in Riyadh, with Dubai a base. Privately held. Leading regional online marketplace with strong consumer awareness across the Gulf and heavy advertising.

wiki.title: Noon
wiki.text: Noon is 12 o'clock in the daytime.

about: Camera and social messaging company behind Snapchat, with augmented reality Lenses, Spectacles smart glasses and Snapchat+ subscriptions. Earns from advertising and subscriptions with about 450 million daily active users, mainly younger demographics. Headquartered in Santa Monica, California; founded 2011. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (SNAP) with revenue around 5 billion dollars. Mass-market consumer app, widely used by teens and young adults, and has run content partnerships with major sports leagues.

wiki.title: Snap Inc.
wiki.text: Snap Inc. is an American technology company, founded in September 2011, by Evan Spiegel, Bobby Murphy, and Reggie Brown, based in Santa Monica, California. The company developed and maintains technological products and services, namely Snapchat, Spectacles (SPECS), and Bitmoji. The company was named Snapchat Inc. at its inception, but it was rebranded Snap Inc. on September 24, 2016, to include the Spectacles (SPECS) product under the company name.

about: Electronic market maker and liquidity provider trading equities, options, futures, fixed income and crypto across more than 50 countries, also providing execution tools and analytics to institutions. Earns from trading spreads and technology services. Headquartered in New York; founded 2008 by Vincent Viola; Virtu also acquired ITG in 2019. Listed on Nasdaq (VIRT). Institutional brand with limited public awareness, but has a motorsport sponsorship link through the Williams Formula 1 team.
cb_desc: Virtuis the global leader in electronic market making.

wiki.title: Virtu Financial
wiki.text: Virtu Financial, Inc. is an American electronic market making company. The company is headquartered in Manhattan, New York City.

about: South Korean internet group behind KakaoTalk, the dominant messenger used by most of the population, plus Kakao Pay, Kakao Bank, Kakao Mobility (taxi), Kakao Entertainment and Melon. Earns from advertising, commerce, fintech and content. Headquartered in Jeju, with main operations in Pangyo near Seoul; founded 2010. Listed on the Korea Exchange (035720). Everyday super-app brand in Korea with extensive consumer reach and mascot licensing (Kakao Friends).

wiki.title: Kakao
wiki.text: Kakao Corporation (Korean: 카카오) is a South Korean internet conglomerate headquartered in Jeju City. It was formed through the merger of Daum Communications and the original Kakao Inc. in 2010. The company was renamed Daum Kakao in 2014. In 2015, it was rebranded once more, reverting simply to Kakao.

about: Atome is a buy now pay later and consumer finance app operating in Southeast Asia, including Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines and Vietnam, plus Hong Kong. Lets shoppers pay in instalments at partner merchants. Part of the Advance Intelligence Group, headquartered in Singapore, also known for AI risk tooling. Funding shown is about 1.5 billion dollars at group level. Consumer brand with strong awareness in the region.
cb_desc: Atome is a financial technology company that provides buy no...

about: Global information services company offering credit reports and scores, fraud prevention, data analytics, marketing services and consumer credit tools such as Experian Boost and CreditWorks. Customers are lenders, retailers, businesses and consumers in about 30 countries, with revenue near 7 billion dollars and about 22,000 employees. Operational headquarters in Costa Mesa, California; Irish-domiciled parent Experian plc is based in Dublin. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (EXPN). Recognised credit bureau brand.

wiki.title: Experian
wiki.what: Irish multinational consumer credit reporting company
wiki.text: Experian plc is a multinational data broker and consumer credit reporting company headquartered in Dublin, Ireland. It is listed on the London Stock Exchange and is a constituent of the FTSE 100 Index. Experian is a partner in USPS address validation. It is one of the "Big Three" alongside TransUnion and Equifax.

about: Data and AI platform company known for the lakehouse architecture, Apache Spark and Delta Lake, which helps enterprises store, analyse and build AI models on their data. Sells subscriptions to large enterprises, with annualised revenue above 4 billion dollars. Headquartered in San Francisco; founded 2013 by the creators of Spark. Private, with funding above 15 billion dollars and a valuation of 100 billion dollars or more. B2B brand known in tech circles with sports partnerships such as Formula 1 team deals.

wiki.title: Databricks
wiki.text: Databricks, Inc. is an American data software and artificial intelligence company headquartered in San Francisco, California. It was founded in 2013 by the original creators of Apache Spark, an open-source framework that was commercialized as Spark through the company. It offers cloud computing-based data analytics solutions, and can run on Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform.

about: Chinese short-video and live streaming platform operator running Kuaishou, with Kwai in international markets, plus e-commerce and the Kling AI video generation model. Earns from advertising, live streaming and e-commerce, with revenue near 18 billion dollars and over 400 million monthly users. Headquartered in Beijing; founded 2011. Listed in Hong Kong (1024), with Tencent as a major shareholder. Very strong consumer brand in China and a sponsor of major events such as the Spring Festival Gala.

wiki.title: Kuaishou
wiki.text: Kuaishou Technology is a Chinese publicly traded partly state-owned holding company based in Haidian District, Beijing, that was founded in 2011 by Su Hua and Cheng Yixiao. The company, listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, is known for developing a mobile app for sharing users' short videos, a social network, and video special effects editor. The app is known as Kwai in many countries outside of China. It is also known as Snack Video in India, Pakistan and Indonesia.

about: Nebius Group is an AI infrastructure and cloud company offering GPU compute, AI cloud services and tools, along with stakes in Avride (autonomous driving), TripleTen (education) and ClickHouse. It was formed from the Dutch parent of Yandex after the Russian business was sold in 2024, and holds a large Microsoft and Meta compute contracts. Headquartered in Amsterdam. Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS). B2B infrastructure brand with limited consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Nebius Group
wiki.text: Nebius Group N.V., headquartered in Amsterdam, is a technology company that provides artificial intelligence infrastructure. It is headquartered in Amsterdam, Netherlands with offices in Israel and the United States.

about: French telecommunications operator formerly France Telecom, providing mobile, broadband, TV and enterprise network services (Orange Business) in France, Spain, Poland, Belgium and across Africa and the Middle East. Serves roughly 290 million customers, with revenue near 40 billion euros and about 125,000 employees. Headquartered in Issy-les-Moulineaux near Paris. Listed on Euronext Paris (ORA), with the French state a large shareholder. Very strong consumer brand and a major sponsor, including of rugby, football, Olympic and cycling events.

wiki.title: Orange Group
wiki.text: Orange S.A. is a French multinational telecommunications corporation founded in 1988 and headquartered in Issy-les-Moulineaux, near Paris.

about: SpaceX AI covers the artificial intelligence business built around xAI, the company founded by Elon Musk in 2023 that makes the Grok chatbot and Colossus supercomputers in Memphis. xAI merged with X in 2025, and SpaceX announced a combination with xAI in early 2026. The input places it in Palo Alto with funding of about 43 billion dollars. Consumers reach Grok through X and its apps. Very high profile but controversial.
cb_desc: SpaceXAl develops Al software and computationa.

wiki.title: SpaceXAI
wiki.what: American artificial intelligence subsidiary of SpaceX
wiki.text: SpaceX Super Intelligence LLC is an American artificial intelligence company founded by Elon Musk. In February 2026, it became a subsidiary of spaceflight company SpaceX, also founded by Musk. SpaceX Super Intelligence's primary products are the Grok family of language, image, and video models; via subsidiaries it operates the X social networking service and Cursor software development environment. The company is headquartered in Palo Alto, with offices in London.

about: Super Micro Computer builds high-performance servers, storage and rack-scale systems, especially GPU-based AI servers using Nvidia chips, with liquid cooling. Customers are cloud providers, data centers, enterprises and AI companies, with revenue of roughly 15 to 20 billion dollars. Headquartered in San Jose, California; founded 1993 by Charles Liang. Listed on Nasdaq (SMCI), with accounting and auditor controversies in 2024. B2B brand with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Supermicro
wiki.what: American supplier of servers and other information technology products
wiki.text: Super Micro Computer, Inc., doing business as Supermicro, is an American information technology company based in San Jose, California. The company is one of the largest producers of high-performance and high-efficiency servers, while also providing server management software, and storage systems for various markets, including enterprise data centers, cloud computing, artificial intelligence, 5G, and edge computing. Supermicro was founded in 1993, and has manufacturing operations in Silicon Valley, the Netherlands, and in Taiwan at its Science and Technology Park.

about: Spanish telecommunications operator providing mobile, broadband, TV and enterprise connectivity under Movistar, O2 and Vivo brands in Spain, Germany, the UK (via the Virgin Media O2 joint venture) and Latin America, especially Brazil. Serves hundreds of millions of customers, with revenue near 40 billion euros. Headquartered in Madrid; founded 1924. Listed on the Madrid exchange (TEF) and New York, with the Spanish state, BBVA and CaixaBank as shareholders. Strong consumer brands and major sports sponsor.

wiki.title: Telefónica
wiki.text: Telefónica, S.A. is a Spanish multinational telecommunications company. It has headquarters as well as a registered office in Madrid, Spain. It is one of the largest telephone operators and mobile network providers in the world. It provides fixed and mobile telephony, broadband, and subscription television, operating in Europe and the Americas.

about: Capgemini is a French IT services and consulting group providing digital transformation, cloud, data, AI, engineering and outsourcing to large enterprises and public bodies in about 50 countries. Revenue near 22 billion euros and over 340,000 employees. Headquartered in Paris; founded 1967. Listed on Euronext Paris (CAP); bought WNS in 2025. B2B brand with strong business recognition, and an active sports sponsor in rugby and tennis.

wiki.title: Capgemini
wiki.text: Capgemini SE is a French multinational information technology (IT) services and consulting company. It is headquartered in Paris, France. The business was established as the Société pour la Gestion de l'Entreprise et le Traitement de l'Information (Sogeti) by Serge Kampf in 1974. It adopted the name CAP Gemini Sogeti in 1975, shortly after it acquired the Centre d'Analyse et de Programmation (CAP) and Gemini Computer Systems. The company expanded considerably during the early 1980s, often via the acquisition of other companies.

about: FICO, Fair Isaac Corporation, is the analytics software company behind the FICO credit score, used by most US lenders, plus decisioning, fraud detection and scoring software. Customers are banks, lenders, insurers and consumers viewing their scores. Revenue near 2 billion dollars. Headquartered in Bozeman, Montana (formerly San Jose); founded 1956. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (FICO). Widely known name in credit but a B2B brand.

wiki.title: FICO
wiki.text: FICO, originally Fair, Isaac and Company, is an American data analytics company based in Bozeman, Montana, focused on credit scoring services. It was founded by Bill Fair and Earl Isaac in 1956. Its FICO score, a measure of consumer credit risk, has become a fixture of consumer lending in the United States.

about: Jefferies Financial Group is a diversified financial holding company whose main business is Jefferies, a global investment bank offering advisory, capital markets, equities and asset management, plus stakes in other businesses. Revenue near 7 billion dollars. Headquartered in New York (input shows Nashville); descended from Leucadia National. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (JEF). Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group is a major shareholder. B2B finance brand with moderate public awareness.

wiki.title: Jefferies Financial Group
wiki.text: Jefferies Financial Group Inc. is an American financial services company based in New York City. It is listed on the New York Stock Exchange and is a part of the Fortune 1000.

about: Ramp is a US corporate spend management platform offering corporate cards, expense management, bill payments and accounting automation, with AI-driven savings features, to businesses from startups to enterprises. Revenue run-rate near 1 billion dollars with tens of thousands of customers. Headquartered in New York; founded 2019 by Eric Glyman and Karim Atiyeh. Private, with a valuation of about 32 billion dollars. Strong B2B brand with sports sponsorship such as Formula 1 team Williams.

wiki.title: Inclined plane
wiki.text: An inclined plane, also known as a ramp, is a flat supporting surface tilted at an angle from the vertical direction, with one end higher than the other, used as an aid for raising or lowering a load. The inclined plane is one of the six classical simple machines defined by Renaissance scientists. Inclined planes are used to move heavy loads over vertical obstacles. Examples vary from a ramp used to load goods into a truck, to a person walking up a pedestrian ramp, to an automobile or railroad train climbing a grade.

wiki.title: Ramp (company)
wiki.text: Ramp Business Corporation is an American multinational financial technology company that offers corporate charge cards, expense management, and bill-payment software. The company is headquartered in New York City with additional offices in Miami and San Francisco.

about: TELUS is Canada's second-largest telecom by revenue, offering mobile, internet, TV, home security and health services plus digital businesses TELUS Health and TELUS Digital (customer support, AI data). Revenue near 20 billion Canadian dollars. Headquartered in Vancouver, British Columbia; formed 1990s from BC Tel. Listed on the Toronto and New York stock exchanges (T). Strong Canadian consumer brand with extensive sports and community sponsorship.

MoonPay is a crypto payments company that lets people buy, sell and swap digital assets with cards and bank transfers through its own app and by embedding its on-ramp in wallets and exchanges, with an NFT and stablecoin business. Headquartered in New York; founded in 2018 by Ivan Soto-Wright and Victor Faramond. Private, funded around 1 billion dollars. Consumer and B2B brand in crypto with big sports and celebrity partnerships.

wiki.title: MoonPay
wiki.text: MoonPay is a multinational financial technology company involved in the transfer of cryptocurrency. Founded by Ivan Soto-Wright, Victor Faramond and Maximilian Crown in 2019, the company is based in Miami and provides payment infrastructure for cryptocurrency and non-fungible tokens (NFTs) to be bought and sold with fiat currencies.

about: Medtronic is one of the world's largest medical device makers, with operational headquarters in Minneapolis and legal base in Galway, Ireland. It sells cardiac devices (pacemakers, defibrillators), diabetes pumps and sensors, surgical robotics, neuromodulation, spine and vascular products to hospitals and health systems in over 150 countries. Revenue is about $32bn with roughly 95,000 employees. Listed on the NYSE (MDT). Primarily B2B and clinician-facing, but a widely recognised healthcare brand; it has used sports sponsorship for awareness, including marathon and cycling links.

wiki.title: Medtronic
wiki.text: Medtronic plc is an international medical device company. The company's legal and executive headquarters are in Ireland, while its operational headquarters are in Minneapolis, Minnesota. Medtronic rebased to Ireland following its acquisition of Irish-based Covidien in 2015. While it primarily operates in the United States, it operates in more than 150 countries and employs over 90,000 people. It develops and manufactures healthcare technologies and therapies. It is one of the biggest medical tech companies in the world and is currently the largest medical device company in the world by revenue.

about: Anysphere is the San Francisco AI company behind Cursor, an AI-powered code editor built on VS Code that helps developers write, edit and debug code using large language models. It sells subscriptions to individual developers and enterprises, and reported annualised revenue above $500m in 2025, growing very quickly. Founded in 2022, it has raised several billion dollars at a valuation reported near $29bn in late 2025, with backers including Thrive, a16z, Accel and Nvidia. Private. Widely known among developers, little mainstream consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Cursor (company)
wiki.text: Anysphere, Inc., doing business as Cursor, is a subsidiary of SpaceXAI which offers generative AI for producing computer code. Its primary product is Cursor, an AI coding agent and software development environment.

about: Unity is a San Francisco software company whose Unity engine is used to build real-time 2D and 3D games and interactive experiences, with products for game monetisation, advertising (Unity Ads, ironSource) and live-ops services. Customers are game developers, studios, automotive, film and industrial firms, paying subscriptions and revenue shares, with annual revenue about $1.8bn. Listed on the NYSE (U). B2B developer tools; widely known to game developers but little consumer brand recognition. It has been involved in motorsport marketing in the past.

wiki.title: Unity Technologies
wiki.text: Unity Software Inc. is an American video game software development company based in San Francisco. It was founded in Denmark in August 2004 as Over the Edge I/S and changed its name in 2007. Unity Technologies is best known for the development of Unity, a licensed game engine used to create video games and other applications.

about: WiseTech Global is a Sydney-area logistics software company whose CargoWise platform runs freight forwarding, customs and supply chain operations for global freight forwarders, carriers and logistics providers. It has grown through many acquisitions, with annual revenue around AUD 1.3-1.4bn and thousands of staff in many countries. Founded by Richard White, it listed on the ASX (WTC) in 2016. B2B software with little consumer awareness; its customers include most of the leading freight forwarders.

wiki.title: Richard White (businessman)
wiki.text: Richard White is the Australian billionaire executive chair, co-founder, and former CEO of WiseTech Global, an Australian technology company specialising in transport logistics.

about: Stats Perform is a Chicago-based sports data, AI and content company supplying live and historical statistics, video, odds and predictive analytics to leagues, broadcasters, teams and betting operators. It was formed in 2019 when STATS merged with Perform Group, owner of the Opta brand. Customers are media groups, clubs, governing bodies and sportsbooks worldwide, and it earns subscription and data licensing fees. Owned by Vista Equity Partners. Private. Opta data is widely seen on TV graphics, though the company brand is B2B.

wiki.title: Stats Perform
wiki.what: British sports technology and data company
wiki.text: Stats Perform is a British sports AI company formed through the merger of Stats and Perform. The company is involved in sports data collection and predictive analysis for use across various sports sectors including professional team performance, digital, media, broadcast and betting. The company began investing in AI in 2015.

about: Wayflyer is a Dublin-based revenue-based financing and growth platform for e-commerce brands, providing funding for inventory and marketing along with analytics. Customers are online merchants across the US, UK, Europe, Canada and Australia, and Wayflyer earns fees on advances. Founded in 2019, it raised a $150m Series B in 2022 and debt facilities, valued at about $1.6bn, with total funding near $3.7bn including debt. Private. B2B fintech with little consumer awareness.

AlphaSense is a New York market intelligence platform using AI to search and summarise company filings, earnings call transcripts, broker research, news and expert call transcripts. Customers are investment banks, hedge funds, asset managers and large corporations, paying subscriptions, with thousands of enterprise clients and revenue reported above $500m. It acquired Tegus in 2024. Private, valued around $4bn after a 2024 round, backed by Goldman Sachs, Viking and others. B2B, known to finance professionals, not consumers.

Autodesk is a San Francisco software company (legal base in San Francisco, with the Autodesk operations in the Bay Area) selling design and engineering tools such as AutoCAD, Revit, Maya, 3ds Max, Fusion and Autodesk Construction Cloud. Customers are architects, engineers, builders, manufacturers and media creators, paying mainly subscriptions, with revenue near $7bn. Listed on Nasdaq (ADSK). Well known to professionals, including film VFX and automotive design teams, and it has partnered with F1 teams on design technology; not a household consumer brand.

wiki.title: Autodesk
wiki.text: Autodesk, Inc. is an American multinational software corporation that provides software products and services for the architecture, engineering, construction, manufacturing, media, education, and entertainment industries. Autodesk is headquartered in San Francisco, California, and has offices worldwide. Its U.S. offices are located in the states of California, Oregon, Colorado, Texas, Michigan, New Hampshire and Massachusetts. Its Canadian offices are located in the provinces of Ontario, Quebec, Alberta, and British Columbia.

about: Canva is an Australian online design platform, headquartered in Sydney (Surry Hills), whose templates, AI tools and drag-and-drop editor let users make presentations, social posts, videos, documents and print designs. It has over 240 million monthly active users in about 190 countries and an annual revenue above $3bn, earned from Pro, Teams and Enterprise subscriptions. Valued at around $42bn in 2025 secondary share sales. Private, founded 2013 by Melanie Perkins. Very recognisable consumer-and-business brand, with sports and F1 partnership activity including a Mercedes-AMG Petronas tie-up.

wiki.title: Canva
wiki.text: Canva Pty Ltd is an Australian multinational software company launched in 2013. The platform provides a graphic design platform to create visual content for presentations, websites, and other digital products. Its uses include templates for presentations, posters, and social media content, as well as photo and video editing functionality.

about: Nuro is a Mountain View, California autonomous driving company, founded in 2016, which built small self-driving delivery vehicles before switching to licensing the Nuro Driver technology to automakers and mobility partners. It has a deal with Uber and Lucid to deploy robotaxis. It has raised over $2bn, including a 2021 round that valued it near $8.6bn, from SoftBank, Google and Nvidia. Private. B2B technology brand with moderate awareness in automotive circles.

wiki.title: Nuro
wiki.text: Nuro, Inc. is an American autonomous vehicle technology company based in Mountain View, California. Founded in 2016 by Jiajun Zhu and Dave Ferguson, Nuro initially developed custom autonomous delivery vehicles and became the first company to receive an autonomous exemption from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA). Since September 2024, the company has focused on licensing its proprietary Level 4 driving system, Nuro Driver, to automakers and mobility providers.

about: OpenText is a Waterloo, Ontario enterprise information management software company, selling content management, cybersecurity, analytics, AI and business network products to large enterprises and governments. It grew through acquisitions including Micro Focus (2023) and Carbonite, with revenue near $5bn and about 22,000 employees. Listed on Nasdaq and the TSX (OTEX). B2B software company with little consumer awareness, though it has run F1-related and team technology partnerships.

wiki.title: OpenText
wiki.text: Open Text Corporation is a global software company that develops and sells information management software.

about: SentinelOne is a Mountain View, California cybersecurity company selling its AI-powered Singularity platform for endpoint, cloud, identity and security data protection to businesses and governments worldwide. It reports annual recurring revenue of around $1bn and thousands of customers. Listed on the NYSE (S) since 2021. B2B brand with little consumer awareness, though it has been active in sports sponsorship.

wiki.title: SentinelOne
wiki.text: SentinelOne, Inc. is an American cybersecurity company listed on NYSE based in Mountain View, California. The company was founded in 2013 by Tomer Weingarten, Almog Cohen and Ehud ("Udi") Shamir. Weingarten acts as the company's CEO. The company has approximately 2,800 employees and offices in Mountain View, Boston, Prague, Tokyo, and Tel Aviv. The company uses machine learning for monitoring personal computers, IoT devices, and cloud workloads. The company's platform utilizes a heuristic model, specifically its patented behavioral AI. The company is AV-TEST certified.

about: Tabby is a Riyadh-based buy-now-pay-later and fintech company serving the Gulf, with the app offering pay-in-4, instalments, cards and a shopping app across Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Kuwait. Founded in the UAE in 2019, it raised $160m in 2025 at a $3.3bn valuation and later reached about $4.5bn in a secondary sale, with Blue Pool, Wellington, PayPal Ventures and others. Private, with a Saudi IPO plan. Strong Gulf consumer brand with heavy advertising and sports sponsorship.

wiki.title: Tabby cat
wiki.what: Domestic cat with distinctive coat markings
wiki.text: A tabby cat, or simply tabby, is any domestic cat with a coat pattern distinguished by an M-shaped marking on its forehead, stripes by its eyes, cheeks, along its back, and around its legs and tail. Tabby cats display characteristic striped, dotted, lined, flecked, banded, or swirled patterns on the body: the neck, shoulders, sides, flanks, or chest. The four known distinct tabby patterns are mackerel, classic, ticked, and spotted. Each is linked to specific genetics.

about: Thomson Reuters is a Toronto-based information and technology company providing legal research (Westlaw), tax and accounting software, news (Reuters) and trade compliance tools to professionals, corporations and governments. It earns subscription revenue of about US$7.3bn and employs about 26,000 people. Majority-controlled by the Thomson family through Woodbridge. Listed on the TSX and Nasdaq (TRI). Mostly B2B, though the Reuters news agency is a globally known brand and it sponsors some events.

wiki.title: Thomson Reuters
wiki.text: Thomson Reuters Corporation is a Canadian multinational content-driven technology conglomerate. The company was founded in Toronto, Ontario, and maintains its headquarters in the city at 19 Duncan Street.

about: Match Group is a Dallas-based (listing shows Los Angeles) online dating company, operating Tinder, Hinge, Match.com, OkCupid, Plenty of Fish, Meetic and Azar, with tens of millions of paying users and revenue near $3.5bn from subscriptions and in-app purchases. Spun off from IAC in 2020 and listed on Nasdaq (MTCH). Very strong consumer brands, particularly Tinder and Hinge, and active in marketing and event partnerships.

wiki.title: Match Group
wiki.text: Match Group, Inc. is an American internet and technology company headquartered in Dallas, Texas. It owns and operates the largest global portfolio of popular online dating services including Tinder, Match.com, Meetic, OkCupid, Hinge, Plenty of Fish, Azar, and other dating global brands. The company was owned by IAC until July 2020 when Match Group was spun off as a separate, public company. As of 2019, the company had 9.3 million subscribers, of which 4.6 million were in North America. Japan is the company's second largest market, after the United States.

about: AppLovin is a Palo Alto software company whose AXON AI advertising engine matches mobile app and e-commerce advertisers with ad inventory, with a legacy portfolio of mobile games now sold to Tripledot. It earns ad network fees from advertisers and publishers, and revenue has grown to around $5bn with high margins. Listed on Nasdaq (APP) and in the S&P 500. B2B ad-tech with little consumer awareness, though well known with investors.

wiki.title: AppLovin
wiki.text: AppLovin Corporation is an American mobile technology company headquartered in Palo Alto, California. Founded in 2012, the company helps developers market, monetize, analyze and publish their apps through its mobile advertising, marketing, and analytics platforms, SSP MAX; DSP AppDiscovery; and SparkLabs creative studio. The company also invests in various mobile game publishers.

about: Celonis is a Munich and New York process mining and execution management software company, helping large organisations analyse how business processes run and fix inefficiencies using its Process Intelligence platform. Customers include Siemens, Uber, Coca-Cola and other large enterprises. It was valued at $13bn in 2022, with total funding around $2.4bn from Accel, 83North and Arena Holdings. Private. B2B software well known to IT leaders and consultants, with little consumer awareness, though it is a known sports sponsor.

wiki.title: Celonis
wiki.text: Celonis SE is a German data processing company that offers software as a service (SaaS) to improve business processes. It is headquartered in Munich, Germany with a secondary headquarters New York, United States.

about: Check Point Software Technologies is a cybersecurity company founded in Israel, with US headquarters in Redwood City and its main office in Tel Aviv, selling network firewalls, cloud security, endpoint, email and threat prevention products (Quantum, Harmony, CloudGuard) to over 100,000 organisations. Revenue is about $2.6bn. Listed on Nasdaq (CHKP). B2B brand with strong IT security recognition, and sponsorship activity including a long-running Formula 1 relationship with Scuderia Ferrari-related partners in the past.

wiki.title: Check Point
wiki.text: Check Point Software Technologies Ltd. is an Israeli cybersecurity company, founded in 1993 by Gil Shwed, Marius Nacht and Shlomo Kramer, whose first product was the FireWall-1 firewall.

about: S&P Global is a New York financial data and analytics group, owning S&P Global Ratings, S&P Global Market Intelligence, S&P Dow Jones Indices (the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average), Platts and Mobility (including CARFAX), and reporting revenue near $14bn. Customers are investors, banks, corporates and governments. Listed on the NYSE (SPGI). Strong B2B brand, with the S&P 500 known to the public, and sponsors in finance and sport.

wiki.title: S&P Global
wiki.text: S&P Global Inc. is an American publicly traded corporation headquartered in Manhattan, New York. Its primary areas of business are financial information, analytics, and energy and commodities intelligence. It is the parent company of S&P Global Ratings, S&P Global Energy, S&P Global Market Intelligence, and the Indian credit rating agency CRISIL. It is also the majority owner of the S&P Dow Jones Indices joint venture. "S&P" is a shortening of "Standard and Poor's."

about: CDW is a Vernon Hills, Illinois-based provider of IT solutions, reselling hardware, software and services from vendors such as Dell, HP, Cisco and Microsoft to business, government, education and healthcare customers in the US, UK and Canada. Founded in 1984, with annual revenue above $20 billion and roughly 15,000 employees. Listed on Nasdaq (CDW). B2B reseller, well known to IT buyers but little consumer awareness; has sponsored sports such as NASCAR and IndyCar.

wiki.title: CDW
wiki.text: CDW Corporation is an American multi-brand provider of information technology services, serving business, government, education, and healthcare sectors across the United States, the United Kingdom, and Canada. Headquartered in Vernon Hills, Illinois, CDW is a Fortune 500 and generated $21 billion in annual net sales in 2023.

about: CGI is a Montreal-based global IT and business consulting firm founded in 1976 by Serge Godin and Andre Imbeau, offering systems integration, managed IT, cybersecurity and consulting to banks, governments, utilities and other large clients. It has about 90,000 employees in 40 countries and annual revenue near C$15 billion. Dual-listed on the TSX and NYSE (GIB). B2B, with limited consumer brand awareness but sponsorship in sports and culture.

wiki.title: CGI Inc.
wiki.text: CGI is a multinational information technology consulting and software development company headquartered in Montreal, Quebec, Canada. CGI went public in 1986 with a primary listing on the Toronto Stock Exchange. CGI is also a constituent of the S&P/TSX 60 and has a secondary listing on the New York Stock Exchange.

about: Saviynt is a Los Angeles-area (Manhattan Beach) cybersecurity company, founded in 2010, providing a cloud-based identity security platform for identity governance, access management and privileged access, with AI features. Customers are large enterprises, government agencies and healthcare organisations. Backed by KKR, which led a $700 million investment in 2025, for a total of roughly $1.1 billion. B2B, little consumer brand awareness.

Safaricom is Kenya's largest telecommunications company, based in Nairobi, offering mobile voice, data, fixed broadband and M-Pesa mobile money, with over 45 million customers in Kenya and Ethiopia (Safaricom Ethiopia). Majority owned by Vodacom (Vodafone) and the government of Kenya, and listed on the Nairobi Securities Exchange (SCOM). Extremely high consumer brand awareness in Kenya and a big sports and events sponsor.

wiki.title: Safaricom
wiki.text: Safaricom PLC is a listed Kenyan mobile network operator headquartered at Safaricom House in Nairobi, Kenya. It is the largest telecommunications provider in Kenya, and one of the most profitable companies in the East and Central Africa region. The company offers mobile telephony, mobile money transfer, consumer electronics, ecommerce, cloud computing, data, music streaming, and fibre optic services. It is most renowned as the home of M-PESA, a mobile banking SMS-based service.

about: Spotify is a Stockholm-based audio streaming company founded in 2006 by Daniel Ek and Martin Lorentzon, with more than 700 million monthly users and over 270 million premium subscribers in about 180 markets, offering music, podcasts and audiobooks. It earns subscriptions and advertising, with annual revenue around 15 billion euros. Listed on NYSE (SPOT). Extremely high consumer brand awareness, and a notable sponsor of football, including the Spotify Camp Nou for FC Barcelona and Wrapped campaigns.

wiki.title: Spotify
wiki.text: Spotify is a Swedish freemium music streaming service provider founded in April 2006 by Daniel Ek and Martin Lorentzon. As of March 2026, it is one of the largest providers of music streaming services, with over 788 million monthly active users comprising 306 million paying subscribers. Spotify is listed on the New York Stock Exchange in the form of American depositary receipts.

about: BT Group is the UK's largest fixed-line and broadband and mobile network operator, headquartered in London, with roughly 100,000 employees. Consumer brands include BT, EE and Plusnet; business unit BT Business and Openreach, the national access network, serve enterprises and wholesale customers. It also offers TV including sports channels such as TNT Sports (a joint venture, formerly BT Sport). Listed on the London Stock Exchange (BT.A) with annual revenue around 20 billion pounds. Very strong UK consumer brand with a history of sports sponsorship.

Palantir Technologies is a US software company founded in 2003, listed on Nasdaq (PLTR) and long headquartered in Denver, Colorado, with the input showing a Miami base. Its Gotham, Foundry and AIP platforms integrate and analyse data for governments, defence and intelligence agencies and large enterprises across health, energy and industry. Revenue exceeds 3 billion dollars annually, growing with AI adoption. B2B brand with strong media and investor profile, and some F1 and commercial partnerships.

wiki.title: Palantir
wiki.text: Palantir Technologies Inc. is an American publicly traded company that develops data integration and analytics software. Palantir is headquartered in Miami, Florida, and was founded in 2003 by Peter Thiel, Stephen Cohen, Joe Lonsdale, Alex Karp, and Nathan Gettings.

about: GoDaddy is a US internet services company headquartered in Tempe, Arizona and listed on the NYSE (GDDY). It is the world's largest domain registrar and sells web hosting, website builder, security, email and commerce tools to about 20 million customers, mostly small businesses and entrepreneurs, with revenue over 4 billion dollars. Founded 1997. Very high consumer awareness through heavy advertising, and a history of sports sponsorships including motorsport.

wiki.title: GoDaddy
wiki.text: GoDaddy Inc. is an American publicly traded Internet domain registry, domain registrar and web hosting company headquartered in Tempe, Arizona, and incorporated under the Delaware General Corporation Law. As of 2023, GoDaddy is the world's fifth-largest web host by market share, with over 62 million registered domains. The company primarily serves small and micro companies, which make up most of its 20 million customers.

about: Harvey is a generative AI platform for legal and professional services firms, built to draft, review and research legal documents. Founded in 2022 and based in San Francisco, it is used by large law firms such as Allen & Overy (now A&O Shearman) and PwC, with backing from OpenAI Startup Fund, Sequoia, Kleiner Perkins and others, at a multi-billion dollar valuation. Customers are law firms and corporate legal departments paying enterprise subscriptions. B2B software with high profile in tech and legal circles but little mass-market awareness.

Walgreens Boots Alliance (WBA) is a US pharmacy and retail healthcare group headquartered in Deerfield, Illinois, formerly listed on Nasdaq (WBA). Its Walgreens and Boots chains operate about 12,000 stores in the US, UK and Europe, alongside Alliance Healthcare wholesale and the VillageMD care business. Revenue is around 140 billion dollars, mostly pharmacy and retail sales. Founded 1901. Sycamore Partners took it private in a deal completed in 2025. Very high consumer visibility, with sports and community partnerships.

wiki.title: Walgreens Boots Alliance
wiki.text: Walgreens Boots Alliance, Inc. (WBA) was an American multinational holding company headquartered in Deerfield, Illinois. The company was formed on December 31, 2014, after Walgreens bought the 55% stake in Alliance Boots that it did not already own. The total price of the acquisition was $4.9 billion in cash and 144.3 million common shares with fair value of $10.7 billion. Walgreens had previously purchased 45% of the company for $4.0 billion and 83.4 million common shares in August 2012 with an option to purchase the remaining shares within three years. Walgreens became a subsidiary of the newly created company after the transactions were co

about: Applied Intuition is a US software company based in Mountain View/Sunnyvale, California providing simulation, validation and vehicle operating system tools for automotive and defence autonomy customers, including many major automakers and the US military. Founded 2017 by former Waymo and Cruise engineers, it raised funding at a valuation of about 15 billion dollars in 2025 and also develops autonomous trucking and software-defined vehicle platforms. Revenue comes from software licences and services. B2B brand known in automotive engineering and defence technology.

wiki.title: Qasar Younis
wiki.text: Qasar Younis is a Pakistani American businessman and venture capitalist who is the CEO and co-founder of Applied Intuition. Prior to Applied Intuition, he was the COO of Y Combinator from 2015 to 2017. He was also the co-founder and CEO of Talkbin.

about: Deel is a global HR and payroll platform that helps companies hire, pay and manage employees and contractors in more than 150 countries. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in San Francisco, it reached a valuation of about 17 billion dollars in 2025, with annualised revenue reported above 1 billion dollars. Customers are businesses of all sizes; money comes from subscription and employer-of-record fees. B2B software brand with a strong tech-sector profile.

wiki.title: Deel, Inc.
wiki.what: Private Delaware-based payroll and compliance provider
wiki.text: Deel, Inc. is an American payroll and human resources company, incorporated in Delaware that operates remotely with a globally distributed workforce. The company provides hiring, payments, and workforce management services for companies hiring international employees and contractors, incorporating artificial intelligence into its software to automate regulatory compliance and administrative tasks. The company was founded in 2019 by Alex Bouaziz, Shuo Wang, and Ofer Simon.

about: Docusign is a US software company headquartered in San Francisco and listed on Nasdaq (DOCU) that pioneered electronic signature and now sells an Intelligent Agreement Management platform for preparing, signing, storing and analysing contracts. It has over a million business customers and revenue near 3 billion dollars from subscriptions. Founded 2003. Well-known B2B brand with a sizeable marketing budget.

wiki.title: Docusign
wiki.text: Docusign, Inc. is an American software company headquartered in San Francisco, California that provides products for organizations to manage electronic agreements and contract lifecycle processes with electronic signatures and AI-supported data extraction on different devices.

about: Keysight Technologies is a US electronic design and test measurement company headquartered in Santa Rosa, California, spun out of Agilent in 2014 and listed on the NYSE (KEYS). It makes oscilloscopes, network analysers, 5G and 6G test systems and cybersecurity validation software for telecoms, automotive, aerospace and electronics customers, with about 15,000 employees and revenue around 5 billion dollars. B2B technology brand known to engineers.

wiki.title: Keysight
wiki.text: Keysight Technologies, Inc. is a global company headquartered in Santa Rosa, California, that makes electronic testing equipment and software used to design, develop, and evaluate technologies. Its customers work in fields including mobile communications, aerospace and defense, automotive manufacturing, semiconductors, digital healthcare, and energy.

about: Mavenir is a US telecom software company based in Richardson, Texas that builds cloud-native and Open RAN network software for mobile operators, including 5G core, voice, messaging and radio, with customers such as Vodafone, Orange and Dish. Owned by Siris Capital since a 2017 take-private, it did a major debt restructuring in 2025. Founded 2005. Revenue is licences and services. B2B telecom supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: Mavenir Systems, Inc.
wiki.text: Mavenir Systems, Inc. is an American telecommunications software company, created in 2017 as a result of a three-way merger of existing companies and technologies, that develops and supplies cloud-native software to the communications service provider (CSP) market.

about: Momenta is a Chinese autonomous driving software company headquartered in Suzhou with offices in Beijing, Shanghai and Munich, founded in 2016. It develops driver-assistance and robotaxi software, supplying automakers such as SAIC and Toyota, and has run robotaxi trials in Shanghai and Germany. Investors include SAIC, Toyota, Mercedes-Benz and Tencent. It has explored a public listing. B2B automotive technology brand with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Momenta
wiki.text: Momenta Global Limited is a developer of intelligent driving technologies, based in Beijing and Suzhou, China.

about: Perplexity is an AI-powered answer engine and search company founded in 2022 and based in San Francisco, which retrieves web results and generates cited answers, with Pro subscriptions, the Comet browser and an API. It serves tens of millions of monthly users and has raised funding at valuations reported near 20 billion dollars from investors including Nvidia and SoftBank. Revenue comes from subscriptions and enterprise plans. Strong tech consumer brand with fast-growing awareness.

wiki.title: Perplexity
wiki.text: In information theory, perplexity is a measurement of how well a probability distribution or probability model predicts a sample. It may be used to compare probability models. A low perplexity indicates the probability distribution is good at predicting the sample.

wiki.title: Perplexity AI
wiki.text: Perplexity AI, Inc., or simply Perplexity, is an American privately held software company offering a web search engine that processes user queries and synthesizes responses. Perplexity products use large language models and include web search capabilities which provide responses based on current Internet content, citing sources used. A free public version is available, while a paid Pro subscription offers access to more advanced language models and additional features.

about: Gen Digital is a US consumer cyber safety company headquartered in Tempe, Arizona and listed on Nasdaq (GEN), formed in 2022 by the merger of NortonLifeLock and Avast. Its brands include Norton, Avast, AVG, LifeLock, Avira, CCleaner and MoneyLion, protecting hundreds of millions of users with antivirus, VPN, identity protection and financial tools, with revenue near 3.9 billion dollars. Descended from Symantec, founded 1982. Very high consumer awareness through direct marketing.

Oura is a Finnish health technology company based in Oulu that makes the Oura Ring, a smart ring that tracks sleep, activity, heart rate and readiness, paired with a membership app. It has sold millions of rings, raising funds at a valuation reported near 11 billion dollars in 2025 with investors such as Fidelity and Dexcom, and has deals with the US military and retailers. Founded 2013. Strong lifestyle wearable brand with celebrity endorsements and sports and wellness partnerships.

wiki.title: Oura Health
wiki.text: Oura Health Ltd is a consumer electronics company founded in 2013. It is headquartered in Oulu, Finland and San Francisco, US.

about: Indra Sistemas is a Spanish technology and defence group headquartered in Madrid and listed on the Spanish stock exchange (IDR, IBEX 35). It develops defence systems, radar, air traffic management, simulation and transport and mobility systems, plus IT consulting through Minsait, serving governments, militaries and companies in 140 countries with revenue near 5 billion euros. The Spanish state, via SEPI, holds a significant stake. Founded 1993. B2B brand known to government and technology buyers.

wiki.title: Indra
wiki.what: Hindu god of rain, lightning, storm and weather
wiki.text: Indra is the Vedic god of weather, considered the king of the devas and the realm of Svarga in Hinduism. He is associated with the sky, lightning, weather, thunder, storms, rains, river flows, and war.

wiki.title: Indra Sistemas
wiki.what: Spanish defense and information tech company
wiki.text: Indra Sistemas, S.A., also known as Indra Group, is a Spanish information technology, transport technology and defense company. Indra is listed on the Bolsa de Madrid and is a constituent of the IBEX 35 index.

about: OSL Group is a Hong Kong-listed digital asset financial services company whose OSL Digital Securities exchange is licensed by Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission to offer crypto trading, brokerage and custody to retail and institutional customers. Formerly BC Group, it is backed by SBI Holdings and others, and has an office in Causeway Bay. Revenue is trading fees. Founded 2018. Crypto-focused brand with moderate profile in Asia.
cb_desc: OSLGroup is a holdingen company that specializes in.

wiki.title: OSL Group
wiki.text: OSL Group is a Hong Kong-based publicly listed company providing services in brokerage, digital assets exchange, over-the-counter trading, and custody of digital assets.

about: OSL Group is a Hong Kong-listed digital asset financial services company whose OSL Digital Securities exchange is licensed by Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission to offer crypto trading, brokerage and custody to retail and institutional customers. Formerly BC Group, it is backed by SBI Holdings and others, and has an office in Causeway Bay. Revenue is trading fees. Founded 2018. Crypto-focused brand with moderate profile in Asia.

wiki.title: OSL Group
wiki.text: OSL Group is a Hong Kong-based publicly listed company providing services in brokerage, digital assets exchange, over-the-counter trading, and custody of digital assets.

about: Wasabi Technologies offers low-cost, S3-compatible hot cloud object storage, positioned as a cheaper alternative to Amazon S3 with no egress fees. Customers are enterprises, media and entertainment firms, managed service providers and backup software partners, billed per terabyte of storage. Founded in 2017 in Boston by the Carbonite founders David Friend and Jeff Flowers. Has raised about $869 million in total funding. Private. Mainly a B2B brand.

wiki.title: Wasabi Technologies
wiki.text: Wasabi Technologies, Inc. is an American object storage service provider based in Boston, Massachusetts that sells cloud storage. The company was co-founded in September 2015 by David Friend and Jeff Flowers and launched its cloud storage product in May 2017.

about: Omio, formerly GoEuro, is a travel booking platform that compares and sells train, bus, flight and ferry tickets across Europe, North America and Asia, covering about 1,000 transport providers. Customers are consumers, and revenue comes from commissions on tickets. Founded in 2012 and headquartered in Berlin, with a large app user base. Crunchbase shows about $606 million in total funding. Private. Recognised consumer travel brand in Europe with significant online marketing.

wiki.title: Omio
wiki.text: Omio is a German online travel agency and multimodal travel booking platform headquartered in Berlin. Founded by Naren Shaam and launched as GoEuro, it enables users to search, compare and book rail, bus and coach, air and ferry travel.

about: Blockchain.com is a crypto platform offering a self-custody wallet, an exchange, institutional trading and a credit card, with tens of millions of wallets created. Founded in 2011 as a Bitcoin block explorer, it is headquartered in London. Revenue comes from trading fees and services. Has raised about $600 million in total funding and was valued around $14 billion in 2022. Private. Recognised crypto consumer brand.

wiki.title: Blockchain.com
wiki.text: Blockchain.com is a cryptocurrency financial services company. The company began as the first Bitcoin blockchain explorer in 2011 and later created a cryptocurrency wallet that accounted for 28% of bitcoin transactions between 2012 and 2020. It also operates a cryptocurrency brokerage and provides institutional markets lending business and data, charts, and analytics.

about: OneFootball is a Berlin-based football media company with a free app serving scores, news, video and live match streaming for millions of fans, particularly in Europe, Brazil and Mexico. Founded in 2008. Revenue comes from advertising, sponsorship, and e-commerce and streaming rights. Crunchbase shows about $442 million in funding. Private. Strong consumer sports media brand with direct access to football fans.

wiki.title: OneFootball
wiki.text: OneFootball is a Berlin-based football media and technology company. Its platform combines live scores, statistics, and news from over 200 leagues in multiple languages through its newsroom in Berlin. In 2019, OneFootball partnered up with Eleven Sports to have the rights to live stream football matches from Spanish first league La Liga in the UK and with Sky to transmit 2. Bundesliga and DFB-Pokal matches in Germany directly through its app. In 2020, OneFootball acquired club-founded video forum Dugout.

about: New York-based observability and security platform for cloud applications, founded 2010, selling monitoring, logs, APM and security tools to engineering teams at about 30,000 customers. Revenue is above $3 billion a year from subscriptions. Listed on Nasdaq (DDOG). B2B brand with strong developer awareness and little consumer recognition, though it is an active sports sponsor. Datadog employs about 7,000 people, and its customers include many of the largest technology companies.

wiki.title: Datadog
wiki.text: Datadog, Inc. is an American company that provides an observability service for cloud-scale applications, providing monitoring of servers, databases, tools, and services, through a SaaS-based data analytics platform. Founded and headquartered in New York City, the company is a publicly traded entity on the Nasdaq stock exchange.

about: San Francisco-based voice, video and text chat platform, founded 2015 as a gaming chat tool and now used by more than 200 million monthly users for communities and friends, earning from Nitro subscriptions, server boosts and ads. Privately held, valued around $15 billion; an IPO has been reported as planned. Strong consumer brand among young gamers and online communities. Discord's users send billions of messages monthly, and the company has about 1,000 employees.

wiki.title: Discord
wiki.text: Discord is an American instant messaging and VoIP social platform that allows communication through voice calls, video calls, text messaging, and media. Communication can be private or in virtual communities called "servers". A server is a collection of persistent chat rooms and voice channels accessed by invitation links. Discord runs on Windows, macOS, Android, iOS, iPadOS, Linux, and in web browsers.

about: Tel Aviv-founded website-building platform, founded 2006, letting small businesses, designers and individuals build sites, stores and apps, and selling domains, hosting and payments. Revenue is above $2 billion, with over 250 million registered users. Listed on Nasdaq (WIX). Strong consumer brand with heavy sports marketing, including football and its appearance in major sponsorships. Wix employs about 5,000 people, and offers tools such as website design, AI builder and payments for small businesses.

Samsung SDS is the IT services and logistics arm of the Samsung group, founded in 1985 and headquartered in Seoul. It provides cloud, system integration, AI, cybersecurity and smart-factory services, plus the Cello Square logistics platform and the Brity enterprise automation brands. Customers are mainly Samsung affiliates and increasingly other large enterprises and governments. It is listed on the Korea Exchange (018260), with Samsung C&T and Samsung Electronics the main shareholders, and revenue around 13 trillion won. B2B, limited consumer awareness, though the Samsung family name is globally strong.

wiki.title: Samsung SDS
wiki.what: South Korean IT company and subsidiary of Samsung Group
wiki.text: Samsung SDS Co., Ltd., Established in 1985 as a subsidiary of Samsung Group, is a provider of Information Technology (IT) services, including consulting, technical, and outsourcing services. SDS is also active in research and development of emerging IT technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), Blockchain, Internet of Things (IoT) and outsourcing in engineering. In 2019, Samsung SDS reported a net profit of 750.4 billion won, an increase of 17.5% year-on-year. The company is estimated to have the 11th most valuable brand among global IT service companies, at US$3.7 billion as of January 2020. Samsung SDS has headquarters in South Kore

about: Brown & Brown is a US insurance brokerage and risk-management group, one of the largest independent brokers in the United States, placing property and casualty, employee benefits and specialty insurance for businesses and individuals through retail, wholesale and programs divisions. Headquartered in Daytona Beach, Florida, it listed on the NYSE (BRO), has more than 17,000 employees and over 4 billion dollars of revenue, and acquired Accession in 2025 for about 9.8 billion dollars. Founded in 1939. Known commercially in the insurance sector, with sports sponsorship in the Daytona area, but with low national consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Brown & Brown
wiki.text: Brown & Brown, Inc. is an American insurance brokerage firm headquartered in Daytona Beach, Florida. It is one of the largest independent insurance intermediaries in the United States, providing risk management solutions, insurance products, and services to businesses, governmental institutions, professional organizations, trade associations, and individuals.

about: Arcelik is a Turkish home appliances manufacturer, a Koc Group company, based in Istanbul, producing white goods and consumer electronics under brands such as Beko, Grundig, Arcelik, Blomberg and Defy. It sells in more than 140 countries, with factories in Turkey, Romania, Russia and elsewhere, and combined its European business with Whirlpool's in 2024. Listed on Borsa Istanbul (ARCLK) with revenue of about 6 billion euros. Beko is a visible consumer brand with football and basketball sponsorship.

wiki.title: Arçelik
wiki.text: Arçelik A.Ş. is a Turkish multinational household appliances manufacturer.

about: Hopper is a Montreal-based travel technology company whose mobile app predicts flight and hotel prices and recommends when to book, selling travel directly through fintech add-ons such as price freeze, cancel for any reason and a Hopper Cloud B2B arm that powers airlines and banks. Founded in 2007, it has over 100 million downloads and has raised about 730 million dollars. Strong awareness among mobile travel shoppers in North America, and heavy performance marketing.

wiki.title: Hopper (company)
wiki.text: Hopper, Inc. is a travel technology company that operates consumer platforms, including the Hopper app and website, and supports partner-branded channels through its business-to-business division, HTS. The company is headquartered in Montreal, Canada, with a major U.S. office in Boston, Massachusetts.

about: Snyk is a Boston-based cybersecurity company, founded in 2015 in London and Tel Aviv, that sells developer-first application security tools, scanning code, open-source dependencies, containers and cloud infrastructure for vulnerabilities. Customers are software teams at enterprises worldwide. It has raised about $1.3 billion, with a peak valuation near $8.5 billion in 2021. B2B brand with strong visibility among developers, little among the general public.

wiki.title: Snyk
wiki.text: Snyk Limited is a developer-oriented cybersecurity company, specializing in securing custom-developed code, open-source dependencies and cloud infrastructure. It was founded in 2015 out of Tel Aviv and London and is headquartered in Boston.

about: Neo4j is a San Mateo, California graph database company, founded in Sweden in 2007, whose software helps companies analyse connected data for fraud detection, recommendations and AI knowledge graphs. Customers include large banks, retailers and governments, paying subscriptions. It has raised about $805 million and was valued at over $2 billion. B2B with strong awareness among developers and data teams.

wiki.title: Neo4j
wiki.text: Neo4j, Inc. is a global graph intelligence company that provides technology for analyzing and managing connected data.

about: Roblox is a San Mateo, California online platform where users build and play millions of user-created 3D games and experiences, listed on the New York Stock Exchange (RBLX). It earns revenue by selling Robux virtual currency and takes a cut from creators, with more than 100 million daily users and revenue above $3.5 billion. Audience is mainly children and teens. Very strong consumer brand, and it works with brand sponsors in virtual worlds.

wiki.title: Roblox
wiki.text: Roblox is an online game platform and game creation system developed by Roblox Corporation that allows users to program and play games created by themselves or other users. It was developed by David Baszucki and Erik Cassel in 2004, and released to the public in 2006. As of February 2025, the platform has reported an average of 85.3 million daily active users. According to the company, its monthly player base includes half of all American children under the age of 16.

about: SS&C Technologies is a Windsor, Connecticut financial software and services company, listed on Nasdaq (SSNC), serving hedge funds, asset managers, banks and insurers with investment accounting, fund administration, trading and healthcare software. It owns Advent, DST and Eze, with revenue of about $6 billion. B2B with little consumer awareness, though it has sponsored sport and golf in the US.

wiki.title: SS&C Technologies
wiki.text: SS&C Technologies Holdings, Inc. is an American multinational holding company headquartered in Windsor, Connecticut, that sells software and software as a service to the financial services industry. The company has offices in the Americas, Europe, Asia, Africa and Australia.

about: ThoughtSpot is a Mountain View, California analytics software company, founded in 2012, offering search- and AI-driven business intelligence so non-technical employees can ask data questions in plain language. Customers are enterprises, paying subscriptions. It has raised about $664 million and was valued at $4.2 billion in 2021. B2B with strong awareness among data teams.

wiki.title: ThoughtSpot
wiki.what: American developer of business intelligence software
wiki.text: ThoughtSpot, Inc. is a technology company that produces business intelligence analytics search software. The company is based in Mountain View, California, and was founded in 2012.

about: OVHcloud is a French cloud computing provider, founded in 1999 in Roubaix by Octave Klaba, offering servers, hosting, private and public cloud and domain services from its own data centers across Europe and elsewhere, and promoting data sovereignty. It listed on Euronext Paris (OVH) in 2021. Customers are developers and enterprises. B2B cloud brand with moderate European awareness.

wiki.title: OVHcloud
wiki.what: French web hosting and cloud computing company
wiki.text: OVHcloud, legally OVH Groupe SA, is a French cloud computing company which offers VPS, dedicated servers, and other web services. The company was founded in 1999 by the Klaba family and is headquartered in Roubaix, France. In 2019 OVH adopted OVHcloud as its public brand name.

about: Workiva is a cloud software company founded in Ames, Iowa that provides Wdesk, a connected reporting and compliance platform used by finance, audit, sustainability and risk teams for SEC filings, ESG reporting and regulatory documents. Customers are thousands of enterprises including a majority of the Fortune 500 who pay subscriptions. Revenue is above 700 million dollars annually. It is listed on the NYSE (WK). It is a B2B software brand with low consumer awareness, though it has sponsored sports properties such as Iowa State.
cb_desc: Workiva created Wdesk, a cloud-based platform for..

wiki.title: Workiva
wiki.text: Workiva, Inc. is a global software-as-a-service (SaaS) company. It provides a cloud-based connected and reporting compliance platform that enables the use of connected data and automation of reporting across finance, accounting, risk, and compliance.

about: Mapbox is a mapping and location data platform company, formed in 2010 and headquartered in San Francisco and Washington, DC. It provides map, navigation, search and geospatial SDKs that developers embed in apps, used by companies such as Snap, the Weather Channel, Instacart and automakers. Revenue is usage-based. SoftBank invested in 2019, and the funding is about $614 million. It is a B2B developer brand with a wide technology profile but little recognition among consumers.

wiki.title: Mapbox
wiki.what: American provider of custom online maps for websites and applications
wiki.text: Mapbox is an American provider of custom online maps for websites and applications such as Foursquare, Lonely Planet, the Financial Times, The Weather Channel, Instacart, and Strava. Since 2010, it has rapidly expanded the niche of custom maps, as a response to the limited choice offered by map providers such as Google Maps.

about: DeepL is a Cologne, Germany AI language company best known for its DeepL Translator, which uses neural networks for text and document translation, plus DeepL Write and voice tools. It sells subscriptions to individuals and enterprise plans, with customers including many large companies. Founded in 2009 as Linguee and rebranded in 2017, it was valued at about 2 billion dollars in 2024 and raised about $400 million. It is a widely known tech brand with a strong user base in Europe.

wiki.title: DeepL Translator
wiki.text: DeepL is a German AI research company known for its language AI platform, which includes DeepL Translator and DeepL Voice, and for DeepL Agent, an AI agent capable of planning workflows and using office systems and tools autonomously, in response to natural language instructions. Its algorithm uses the transformer architecture. It offers a paid subscription for additional features and access to its translation application programming interface. DeepL was founded in 2017 by Jaroslaw Kutylowski and is a unicorn, valued at $2 billion after a Series C funding round raised $300 million in May 2024. Its more than 200,000 business customers include

about: Pentera is a cybersecurity company, originally from Israel (Petah Tikva) with a US base listed in Burlington, Massachusetts, that offers an automated security validation platform which continuously simulates real attacks to find exploitable weaknesses. Customers are large enterprises and financial institutions around the world. Founded in 2015, it was valued above 1 billion dollars in 2021 and has raised about $250 million. It is a B2B security brand with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Pentera
wiki.text: Pentera, formerly known as Pcysys, is a cybersecurity software company based in Boston. It has operations in the United States, Germany, the UK, Israel, Dubai, and Singapore.

about: Motorola Solutions provides mission-critical communications and public safety technology: land mobile radios, body cameras, video security (Avigilon), command centre software and emergency call handling for police, fire, ambulance and enterprises. It was formed in 2011 when Motorola Inc. split into Motorola Solutions and Motorola Mobility. Headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, with about 21,000 employees and roughly 10 billion dollars in revenue. Listed on the NYSE (MSI). Customers are governments and enterprises worldwide. The Motorola name is widely known; the company has sports partnerships including security and communications services.

wiki.title: Motorola Solutions
wiki.text: Motorola Solutions, Inc., is an American technology company that provides safety and security products and services. Headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, the company provides critical communications, video security, and command center technologies, used by public safety agencies and enterprises. It was formed in 2011 by the division of Motorola, Inc., and is its legal successor; the former company's mobile phone division was spun off as Motorola Mobility, now part of Chinese technology company Lenovo.

about: o9 Solutions is a Dallas-based provider of cloud planning software, the o9 Digital Brain platform, for demand planning, supply chain, revenue management and integrated business planning, used by large consumer goods, retail and industrial companies. Founded in 2009 by Sanjiv Sidhu, it was valued at about 3.7 billion dollars in 2021, backed by KKR, Generation Investment Management and others. B2B enterprise software, known in supply chain circles, with no consumer visibility.

Polygon is a blockchain network and ecosystem for scaling Ethereum, launched in 2017 as Matic Network by founders in India and used by apps such as Aave and Uniswap and by brand projects from companies such as Starbucks, Nike and Reddit. Its POL token supports Polygon PoS, zkEVM and the AggLayer. The company has been backed by Sequoia India and Tiger Global, among others. Known in crypto circles, where it has done sports partnerships.

wiki.title: Polygon
wiki.what: Plane figure bounded by line segments
wiki.text: In geometry, a polygon is a plane figure made up of line segments connected to form a closed polygonal chain.

about: MongoDB is a New York-headquartered database software company known for its document database, offered as MongoDB Atlas on the cloud and on premises, with vector search for AI applications. Founded in 2007 as 10gen by Dwight Merriman, Eliot Horowitz and Kevin Ryan, it has over 50,000 customers and revenue near 2 billion dollars. Listed on Nasdaq (MDB). B2B developer brand with very strong awareness among software engineers, but little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: MongoDB
wiki.text: MongoDB is a source-available, cross-platform, document-oriented database program. Classified as a NoSQL database product, MongoDB uses JSON-like documents with optional schemas. Released in February 2009 by 10gen, it supports features like sharding, replication, and ACID transactions. MongoDB Atlas, its managed cloud service, operates on AWS, Google Cloud Platform, and Microsoft Azure. Current versions are licensed under the Server Side Public License (SSPL). MongoDB is a member of the MACH Alliance.

about: PTC is a Boston-area industrial software company, listed on Nasdaq (PTC), founded in 1985, whose products include Creo CAD, Windchill product lifecycle management, ThingWorx for industrial IoT, Onshape cloud CAD and Vuforia augmented reality. Customers are manufacturers in automotive, aerospace, medical devices and industrial equipment, who pay subscription fees. Revenue is about $2.5 billion. B2B software brand, widely known among engineers and manufacturers but not among consumers.

Ziff Davis is a New York digital media and internet company, listed on Nasdaq (ZD). It owns a portfolio of web brands and services, including IGN, Mashable, PCMag, CNET, Everyday Health, Speedtest by Ookla, and cybersecurity, email marketing and cloud businesses. Revenue comes from advertising, subscriptions, lead generation and licensing, serving consumers and technology and healthcare marketers. It has over a billion monthly visits across its sites and annual revenue around 1.4 billion dollars. Several of its media brands, especially IGN and CNET, are well known to tech and gaming audiences.

wiki.title: Ziff Davis
wiki.text: Ziff Davis, Inc. is an American digital media and Internet company. Founded in 1927 by William Bernard Ziff Sr. and Bernard George Davis, the company primarily owns technology- and health-oriented media websites, online shopping-related services, Internet connectivity services, gaming and entertainment brands, and cybersecurity and martech tools. Previously, the company was predominantly a publisher of hobbyist magazines.
